question: Catalonia’s Decree-Law 3/2023 introduced an authorisation scheme and a de facto temporary ban on short-term leases. The authorities maintain that this curtailing of the freedom to provide services is justified by an overriding public-interest reason.
These restrictions, however fly in the face of the principle of proportionality, which requires that measures be appropriate and not exceed what is necessary to achieve the objective pursued.

In particular, the authorities have: (i) Failed to show a causal link between short-term leases and the housing crisis; (ii) imposed restrictions that disproportionately affect tourist accommodation for an equally disproportionate period of five years; and (iii) failed to consider less restrictive measures. Given these circumstances: 1.
What view does the Commission take of these measures given Articles 10, 14(5), 15(3)(c) and 16(1)(c) of the Services Directive and the Commission’s guidelines1?
Does the Commission consider that Decree-Law 3/2023 might infringe EU law by imposing restrictions that could go beyond what is necessary to achieve the intended objective?
Ref. Ares(2018)5381503.
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (21.9.2026) Decree-law 3/2023, adopted by the Catalonian government on 7 November 2023, was notified to the Commission pursuant to the Services Directive1 and using the Internal Market Information System (‘the IMI’).

This Decree-law made dwellings of touristic use in Catalonia subject to a prior urban planning permission, valid for five years and extendable for subsequent periods of five years, in municipalities that fulfilled certain conditions, which at the time of its adoption amounted to 262 of them.

On 18 December 2023, the Commission services issued comments on the notified Decree-law, focusing on the assessment of the suitability of the restrictions to attain the objective of fighting housing shortage and, more broadly, their proportionality on account of their wide geographical scope. The Catalonian Government submitted its reply, via the IMI, on 18 January 2024.

The Commission is currently assessing restrictions on short-term accommodation rentals in several Spanish autonomous communities and cities, including Catalonia and Barcelona, and Member States other than Spain.

Any decisions will follow a consistent approach, considering the objectives of the European Affordable Housing Plan2 and the recently tabled Commission’s proposal for an Affordable Housing Act3, which seeks to provide legal certainty on justified and proportionate measures that authorities can take to temporarily protect housing markets.
